e-4810.knowledge_point: Identifying Whether a Vector Lies in the Null Space of a Given Matrix
e-4810.problem:
The matrix $A$ and vectors $\mathbf{b}_1$, $\mathbf{b}_2$, $\mathbf{b}_3$ are given below. Which of the vectors lie in $\textrm{Null}(A)?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064430/assets/9832b17728be69381a5f534317c0f30156fd32f3706f4cd4634765a02370180e.png)
e-4810.worked_solution:
A vector $\mathbf{b}$ lies in $\textrm{Null}(A)$ if $A\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{0}.$ So, we need to compute the product of $A$ and each of the given vectors and check whether it is equal to $\mathbf{0}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}A{b}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 \\ -5 & 10 \\ -8 & 16\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-27 \\ 45 \\ 72\end{aligned}]\ne 0\,\times  \\ A{b}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 \\ -5 & 10 \\ -8 & 16\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=0\,✓ \\ A{b}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 \\ -5 & 10 \\ -8 & 16\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-15 \\ 25 \\ 40\end{aligned}]\ne 0\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, only $\mathbf{b}_2$ lies in $\textrm{Null}(A).$

e-4812.knowledge_point: Solve a Variable in a Vector Lying in the Null Space of a Given Matrix
e-4812.problem: Consider the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064430/assets/a8b13d238a1e77d90abe70a505c68a72060ea95fe545f56ae53e7cf40ba0595e.png) and the vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064430/assets/6e9f6c010c3137438923dfc32674dedf6d2d554b9b0a6745b007d826954d1e65.png) Find the value of $k$ such that $\mathbf{b}\in\textrm{Null}(A).$
e-4812.worked_solution:
If $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Null}(A),$ then we must have $A\mathbf{b} = \mathbf{0}.$ Substituting the given information, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Ab & =0 \\ [\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -4 \\ -3 & 3 & -1 \\ 6 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ k \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}6+2k-12 \\ -6+3k-3 \\ 12-6k+6\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}2k-6=0 \\ 3k-9=0 \\ -6k+18=0\end{aligned}
$$

and for each of these equations, we obtain $k=3.$

e-4814.knowledge_point: Finding the Null Space of a Given Matrix
e-4814.worked_solution:
We need to solve the equation $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}.$ First, we find the row echelon form of $A$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -12 \\ 3 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 3 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

The second equation tells us that $x_2=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} & =0 \\ {x}_{1}-3(0) & =0 \\ {x}_{1} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064430/assets/f73d7951a041c633d78d1d6971a3473800727452bb92e1b39ad574a045e1b76f.png) is the only solution to this system.

Therefore, $\textrm{Null}(A) = \left\{ \mathbf{0} \right\}.$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
The matrix $A$ and vectors ${b}_{1}$, ${b}_{2}$, ${b}_{3}$ are given below. Which of the vectors lie in $\text{Null}(A)?$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -4 & 2 \\ 6 & -3\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$
after.worked_solution:
A vector $b$ lies in $\text{Null}(A)$ if $Ab=0.$ So, we need to compute the product of $A$ and each of the given vectors and check whether it is equal to $0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A{b}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -4 & 2 \\ 6 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=0\,✓ \\ A{b}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -4 & 2 \\ 6 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 10 \\ -15\end{aligned}]\ne 0\,\times  \\ A{b}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -4 & 2 \\ 6 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, only ${b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{3}$ lie in $\text{Null}(A).$

content.problem:
The matrix $A$ and vectors ${b}_{1}$, ${b}_{2}$, ${b}_{3}$ are given below. Which of the vectors lie in $\text{Null}(A)?$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -4 & 2 \\ 6 & -3\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]

content.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}A{b}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -4 & 2 \\ 6 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=0\,✓ \\ A{b}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -4 & 2 \\ 6 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 10 \\ -15\end{aligned}]\ne 0\,\times  \\ A{b}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -4 & 2 \\ 6 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=0\,✓\end{aligned}

Therefore, only ${b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{3}$ lie in $\text{Null}(A).$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
The matrix $A$ and vectors ${b}_{1}$, ${b}_{2}$, ${b}_{3}$ are given below. Which of the vectors lie in $\text{Null}(A)?$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -5 & 4 \\ 6 & -10 & 8\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$
after.worked_solution:
A vector $b$ lies in $\text{Null}(A)$ if $Ab=0.$ So, we need to compute the product of $A$ and each of the given vectors and check whether it is equal to $0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A{b}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -5 & 4 \\ 6 & -10 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}41 \\ 82\end{aligned}]\ne 0\,\times  \\ A{b}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -5 & 4 \\ 6 & -10 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8 \\ 7\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=0\,✓ \\ A{b}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -5 & 4 \\ 6 & -10 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 14\end{aligned}]\ne 0\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, only ${b}_{2}$ lies in $\text{Null}(A).$

A vector b lies in Null(A) if Ab=0. So, we need to compute the product of A and each of the given vectors and check whether it is equal to 0:

Ab1=[3−71−1][6−3]=[399]≠0×Ab2=[3−71−1][2−4]=[346]≠0×Ab3=[3−71−1][−43]=[−33−7]≠0×

after.name: Question 6
after.problem: Consider the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}28 & -7 & 14 \\ -4 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]$ and the vector $b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ k \\ -1\end{aligned}].$ Find the value of $k$ such that $b\in \text{Null}(A).$
after.worked_solution:
If $b\in \text{Null}(A),$ then we must have $Ab=0.$ Substituting the given information, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Ab & =0 \\ [\begin{aligned}28 & -7 & 14 \\ -4 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ k \\ -1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-7k+14 \\ k-2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-7k+14=0 \\ k-2=0\end{aligned}
$$

and for each of these equations, we obtain $k=2.$

content.problem: Consider the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -8 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}]$ and the vector $b=[\begin{aligned}k \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Find the value of $k$ such that $b\in \text{Null}(A).$
content.worked_solution:
If $b\in \text{Null}(A),$ then we must have $Ab=0.$ Substituting the given information, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Ab & =0 \\ [\begin{aligned}-2 & -8 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}k \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-2k-8 \\ k+4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2k-8=0 \\ k+4=0\end{aligned}
$$

and for each of these equations, we obtain $k=-4.$

before.html:
Question 11
?

Consider the matrix A=[1−25−24−103−615]. Find Null(A).

a
{[2x2−5x3x2x3]:x2,x3∈R}
b
{[5x2−2x3x2x3]:x2,x3∈R}
c
{[2x2+5x3x2x3]:x2,x3∈R}
d
{[5x2+2x3x2x3]:x2,x3∈R}
e
{0}
Submit

decision.explanation: The second and third rows are multiples of the first, so Ax=0 reduces to x₁−2x₂+5x₃=0. Thus x₁=2x₂−5x₃, with x₂ and x₃ arbitrary real numbers.

after.name: Question 11
after.worked_solution:
We need to solve the equation $Ax=0.$ First, we find the row echelon form of $A$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 5 \\ -2 & 4 & -10 \\ 3 & -6 & 15\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & -6 & 15\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}+5{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is ${x}_{1}$, and we have two free variables, ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}.$ That means we need to find ${x}_{1}$ in terms of ${x}_{2}$  and ${x}_{3}.$

From the first equation we get ${x}_{1}=2{x}_{2}-5{x}_{3},$ so the set of all the solutions of $Ax=0$ is

$$
\text{Null}(A)={[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2}-5{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R}.
$$

Question 11
?

Consider the matrix A=[1−25−24−103−615]. Find Null(A).

a
{[2x2−5x3x2x3]:x2,x3∈R}
b
{[5x2−2x3x2x3]:x2,x3∈R}
c
{[2x2+5x3x2x3]:x2,x3∈R}
d
{[5x2+2x3x2x3]:x2,x3∈R}
e
{0}
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need to solve the equation Ax=0. First, we find the row echelon form of A as follows:

A=[1−25−24−103−615]R2:=R2+2R1∼[1−250003−615]R3:=R3+(−3)R1∼[1−25000000]

This corresponds to the following system:

{x1−2x2+5x3=00=00=0

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is x1, and we have two free variables, x2 and x3. That means we need to find x1 in terms of x2 and x3.

From the first equation we get x1=2x2−5x3, so the set of all the solutions of Ax=0 is

Null(A)={[2x2−5x3x2x3]:x2,x3∈R}.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Null Space of a Given Matrix
content.worked_solution:
We need to solve the equation $Ax=0.$ First, we find the row echelon form of $A$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 5 \\ -2 & 4 & -10 \\ 3 & -6 & 15\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & -6 & 15\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}+5{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is ${x}_{1}$, and we have two free variables, ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}.$ That means we need to find ${x}_{1}$ in terms of ${x}_{2}$  and ${x}_{3}.$

From the first equation we get ${x}_{1}=2{x}_{2}-5{x}_{3},$ so the set of all the solutions of $Ax=0$ is

$$
\text{Null}(A)={[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2}-5{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R}.
$$

Question 12
?

Consider the matrix A=[3694984812]. Find Null(A).

a
{[−11x34x3x3]:x3∈R}
b
{[−11x2x24x2]:x2∈R}
c
{0}
d
{[x14x1−11x1]:x1∈R}
e
{[4x3−11x3x3]:x3∈R}
Submit

decision.explanation: The first equation gives x₁+2x₂+3x₃=0. Subtracting four times this equation from the second gives x₂−4x₃=0. Thus x₂=4x₃ and x₁=−11x₃; the third equation repeats the first.

after.name: Question 12
after.worked_solution:
We need to solve the equation $Ax=0.$ First, we find the row echelon form of $A$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 & 9 \\ 4 & 9 & 8 \\ 4 & 8 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 9 & 8 \\ 4 & 8 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 \\ 4 & 8 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{2}-4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$, and we have one free variables, ${x}_{3}.$ That means we need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ in terms of ${x}_{3}.$

From the second equation we get ${x}_{2}=4{x}_{3}.$ Substituting ${x}_{2}=4{x}_{3}$ into the first equation, we get 

$$
{x}_{1}+2(4{x}_{3})+3{x}_{3}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-11{x}_{3}.
$$

So the set of all the solutions of $Ax=0$ is

$$
\text{Null}(A)={[\begin{aligned}-11{x}_{3} \\ 4{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{3}\in R}.
$$

Consider the matrix A=[3694984812]. Find Null(A).

a
{[−11x34x3x3]:x3∈R}
b
{[−11x2x24x2]:x2∈R}
c
{0}
d
{[x14x1−11x1]:x1∈R}
e
{[4x3−11x3x3]:x3∈R}
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We need to solve the equation Ax=0. First, we find the row echelon form of A as follows:

A=[3694984812]R1:=13R1∼[1234984812]R2:=R2+(−4)R1∼[12301−44812]R3:=R3+(−4)R1∼[12301−4000]

This corresponds to the following system: {x1+2x2+3x3=0x2−4x3=00=0

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are x1 and x2, and we have one free variables, x3. That means we need to find x1 and x2 in terms of x3.

From the second equation we get x2=4x3. Substituting x2=4x3 into the first equation, we get

x1+2(4x3)+3x3=0⟹x1=−11x3.

So the set of all the solutions of Ax=0 is

Null(A)={[−11x34x3x3]:x3∈R}.

content.worked_solution:
We need to solve the equation $Ax=0.$ First, we find the row echelon form of $A$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 & 9 \\ 4 & 9 & 8 \\ 4 & 8 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 9 & 8 \\ 4 & 8 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 \\ 4 & 8 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{2}-4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$, and we have one free variables, ${x}_{3}.$ That means we need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ in terms of ${x}_{3}.$

From the second equation we get ${x}_{2}=4{x}_{3}.$ Substituting ${x}_{2}=4{x}_{3}$ into the first equation, we get 

$$
{x}_{1}+2(4{x}_{3})+3{x}_{3}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-11{x}_{3}.
$$

So the set of all the solutions of $Ax=0$ is

$$
\text{Null}(A)={[\begin{aligned}-11{x}_{3} \\ 4{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{3}\in R}.
$$

Question 13
?

Consider the matrix A=[−13−25−15102−64]. Find Null(A).

a
{0}
b
{[3x2−2x311]:x2,x3∈R}
c
{[x2−5x3x2x3]:x2,x3∈R}
d
{[3x2−2x340]:x2,x3∈R}
e
{[3x2−2x3x2x3]:x2,x3∈R}
Submit

decision.explanation: The second and third rows are multiples of the first, so Ax=0 reduces to −x₁+3x₂−2x₃=0. Therefore x₁=3x₂−2x₃, with x₂ and x₃ arbitrary real numbers.

after.name: Question 13
after.worked_solution:
We need to solve the equation $Ax=0.$ First, we find the row echelon form of $A$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & -2 \\ 5 & -15 & 10 \\ 2 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 \\ 5 & -15 & 10 \\ 2 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is ${x}_{1}$, and we have two free variables, ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}.$ That means we need to find ${x}_{1}$ in terms of ${x}_{2}$  and ${x}_{3}.$

From the first equation we get ${x}_{1}=3{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3},$ so the set of all the solutions of $Ax=0$ is

$$
\text{Null}(A)={[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R}.
$$

Question 13
?

Consider the matrix A=[−13−25−15102−64]. Find Null(A).

a
{0}
b
{[3x2−2x311]:x2,x3∈R}
c
{[x2−5x3x2x3]:x2,x3∈R}
d
{[3x2−2x340]:x2,x3∈R}
e
{[3x2−2x3x2x3]:x2,x3∈R}
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need to solve the equation Ax=0. First, we find the row echelon form of A as follows:

A=[−13−25−15102−64]R1:=(−1)R1∼[1−325−15102−64]R2:=R2+(−5)R1∼[1−320002−64]R3:=R3+(−2)R1∼[1−32000000]

This corresponds to the following system:

{x1−3x2+2x3=00=00=0

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is x1, and we have two free variables, x2 and x3. That means we need to find x1 in terms of x2 and x3.

From the first equation we get x1=3x2−2x3, so the set of all the solutions of Ax=0 is

Null(A)={[3x2−2x3x2x3]:x2,x3∈R}.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Null Space of a Given Matrix
content.worked_solution:
We need to solve the equation $Ax=0.$ First, we find the row echelon form of $A$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & -2 \\ 5 & -15 & 10 \\ 2 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 \\ 5 & -15 & 10 \\ 2 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is ${x}_{1}$, and we have two free variables, ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}.$ That means we need to find ${x}_{1}$ in terms of ${x}_{2}$  and ${x}_{3}.$

From the first equation we get ${x}_{1}=3{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3},$ so the set of all the solutions of $Ax=0$ is

$$
\text{Null}(A)={[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R}.
$$

decision.explanation: The second row is twice the first, so Ax=0 reduces to 3x₁+6x₂=0. Thus x₁=−2x₂, with x₂ any real number.

after.name: Question 14
after.worked_solution:
We need to solve the equation $Ax=0.$ First, we find the row echelon form of $A$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 \\ 6 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 6 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-6){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is ${x}_{1}$, and we have one free variable, ${x}_{2}.$ That means we need to find ${x}_{1}$ in terms of ${x}_{2}.$

From the first equation we get ${x}_{1}=-2{x}_{2},$ so the set of all the solutions of $Ax=0$ is

$$
\text{Null}(A)={[\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{2}\in R}.
$$

Consider the matrix A=[−39−96−18183−89]. Find Null(A).

a
{[−3x3x3x3]:x3∈R}
b
{0}

{[3x30x3]:x3∈R}
d
{[−3x30x3]:x3∈R}

decision.explanation: Adding the first and third equations of Ax=0 gives x₂=0. The first then gives −3x₁−9x₃=0, so x₁=−3x₃. The second equation is a multiple of the first, leaving x₃ free.

after.name: Question 15
after.worked_solution:
We need to solve the equation $Ax=0.$ First, we find the row echelon form of $A$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 & -9 \\ 6 & -18 & 18 \\ 3 & -8 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 3 \\ 6 & -18 & 18 \\ 3 & -8 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-6){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & -8 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{2}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$, and we have one free variable, ${x}_{3}.$ That means we need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ in terms of ${x}_{3}.$

The second equation tells us that ${x}_{2}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get 

$$
{x}_{1}-3(0)+3{x}_{3}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-3{x}_{3}.
$$

So the set of all the solutions of $Ax=0$ is

$$
\text{Null}(A)={[\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{3} \\ 0 \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{3}\in R}.
$$

Question 15
?

Consider the matrix A=[−39−96−18183−89]. Find Null(A).

a
{[−3x3x3x3]:x3∈R}
b
{0}
c
{[3x30x3]:x3∈R}
d
{[−3x30x3]:x3∈R}
e
{[3x3x3x3]:x3∈R}
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need to solve the equation Ax=0. First, we find the row echelon form of A as follows:

A=[−39−96−18183−89]R1:=−13R1∼[1−336−18183−89]R2:=R2+(−6)R1∼[1−330003−89]R3:=R3+(−3)R1∼[1−33000010]R2↔R3∼[1−33010000]

This corresponds to the following system:

{x1−3x2+3x3=0x2=00=0

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are x1 and x2, and we have one free variable, x3. That means we need to find x1 and x2 in terms of x3.

The second equation tells us that x2=0. Substituting this into the first equation, we get

x1−3(0)+3x3=0⟹x1=−3x3.

So the set of all the solutions of Ax=0 is

Null(A)={[−3x30x3]:x3∈R}.

content.worked_solution:
We need to solve the equation $Ax=0.$ First, we find the row echelon form of $A$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 & -9 \\ 6 & -18 & 18 \\ 3 & -8 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 3 \\ 6 & -18 & 18 \\ 3 & -8 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-6){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & -8 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{2}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$, and we have one free variable, ${x}_{3}.$ That means we need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ in terms of ${x}_{3}.$

The second equation tells us that ${x}_{2}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get 

$$
{x}_{1}-3(0)+3{x}_{3}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-3{x}_{3}.
$$

So the set of all the solutions of $Ax=0$ is

$$
\text{Null}(A)={[\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{3} \\ 0 \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{3}\in R}.
$$
